input.command:
import requests, json, statistics
base="https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data/activity.json"
params={"molecule_chembl_id":"CHEMBL941","target_chembl_id":"CHEMBL1862","limit":1000}
r=requests.get(base,params=params,timeout=120)
print(r.status_code, r.url)
d=r.json()
acts=d["activities"]
print("n=",len(acts), d["page_meta"]["total_count"])
from collections import Counter
print(Counter([(a["standard_type"],a["standard_units"]) for a in acts]))

t=requests.get("https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data/target/CHEMBL1862.json",timeout=60).json()
print(t["pref_name"], t["target_type"], t["organism"], [c["accession"] for c in t["target_components"]])

ic=[float(a["standard_value"]) for a in acts if a["standard_type"]=="IC50" and a["standard_units"]=="nM" and a["standard_value"]]
kd=[float(a["standard_value"]) for a in acts if a["standard_type"]=="Kd" and a["standard_units"]=="nM" and a["standard_value"]]
ki=[float(a["standard_value"]) for a in acts if a["standard_type"]=="Ki" and a["standard_units"]=="nM" and a["standard_value"]]
for name,v in [("IC50",ic),("Kd",kd),("Ki",ki)]:
    v=sorted(v)
    print(name,"n=",len(v),"median=",statistics.median(v),"min=",v[0],"max=",v[-1])

def show(tp):
    rows=[a for a in acts if a["standard_type"]==tp and a["standard_units"]=="nM" and a["standard_value"]]
    rows.sort(key=lambda a: float(a["standard_value"]))
    for a in rows:
        print(f'{a["standard_value"]:>9} nM | {a["assay_chembl_id"]} | {a["assay_type"]} | {a["bao_label"]} | {str(a["assay_description"])[:110]} | {a["document_chembl_id"]}')
print("=== Kd ===");show("Kd")
print("\n=== Ki ===");show("Ki")

for tp in ["IC50","Kd","Ki"]: wt(tp)

# Guide to PHARMACOLOGY

print([(x["ligandId"],x["name"]) for x in g])

content.text:
## What I did

I queried the ChEMBL REST API (`https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data/activity.json`) for every recorded activity linking imatinib to ABL1, using the Python REPL tool (`mcp__biomni__run_python_repl`):

- **Compound:** CHEMBL941 (imatinib)
- **Target:** CHEMBL1862 — "Tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1", SINGLE PROTEIN, *Homo sapiens*, UniProt **P00519** (confirmed via the ChEMBL target endpoint)
- **Records returned:** 160 total activities

Breakdown by measurement type: IC50 n=91 (nM), Kd n=31, Ki n=6, plus kinetics (kon/koff), % inhibition and GI50.

Important caveat about this set: ChEMBL maps **mutant** ABL1 assays (T315I, Y253F, E255K, M351T, H396P, F317L…) onto the same wild-type target ID, and T315I is imatinib-resistant. Including them drags the IC50 median to 800 nM. Filtering assay descriptions to wild-type / unphosphorylated-native ABL1 only:

| Type | n (WT only) | Median | Geometric mean | Range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IC50 | 37 | **223 nM** | 213 nM | 19.9 – 2700 nM |
| Ki | 4 | 13 nM | 18 nM | 13 – 50 nM |
| Kd | 4 | 7.1 nM | 7.3 nM | 1.0 – 106 nM |

Representative single records (all retrieved from ChEMBL, assay IDs given so you can cite them):

- **IC50 = 170 nM** — CHEMBL3737992, enzymatic radiometric phosphocellulose paper-disk assay, 0.1 mM EAIYAAPFAKKK peptide substrate, 30 min; pChEMBL 6.77 (doc CHEMBL3734755)
- **IC50 = 19.9 nM** — CHEMBL2406231, TR-FRET, His-ABL 229–513 from *E. coli*, 30–60 min pre-incubation, biotinyl-poly(Glu-Tyr) substrate; pChEMBL 7.70. The ~10× spread vs. the above is the usual ATP-concentration / pre-incubation / substrate dependence
- **Ki = 13 nM** — CHEMBL932076 / CHEMBL962773, filter-binding assay on human recombinant Abl; pChEMBL 7.89
- **Kd = 1.1 nM** — CHEMBL1908688, competition binding against the **non-phosphorylated** ABL1 kinase domain; pChEMBL 8.96. The same study gives Kd = 21 nM for the **phosphorylated** kinase domain — imatinib only binds the inactive/DFG-out conformation, which is the main reason binding and enzymatic numbers diverge
- **Cellular GI50 = 260 nM** — CHEMBL4383405, TEL-ABL-transformed BA/F3 proliferation

Two things I could not do: the Guide to PHARMACOLOGY REST service now returns HTTP 401 ("API key is missing"), and the `query_gtopdb` tool failed with a response-parsing error, so I have no GtoPdb-sourced number to cross-check with. These are database lookups, not predictions, so there is no model confidence to report; the pChEMBL values above are ChEMBL's own −log10 transforms of the reported potencies.

## ANSWER

**IC50 = 170 nM** against wild-type human ABL1 (ChEMBL assay CHEMBL3737992; enzymatic radiometric phosphocellulose paper-disk kinase assay, EAIYAAPFAKKK peptide substrate; pChEMBL 6.77).

Consistent alternatives from the same target record (CHEMBL1862 / UniProt P00519, compound CHEMBL941):
- Ki = 13 nM — filter-binding enzyme assay (CHEMBL932076)
- Kd = 1.1 nM — competition binding, non-phosphorylated ABL1 kinase domain (CHEMBL1908688)
- Wild-type IC50 consensus across 37 ChEMBL assays: median 223 nM (range 19.9–2700 nM)

| Type | n (WT only) | Median | Geometric mean | Range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IC50 | 37 | **223 nM** | 213 nM | 19.9 – 2700 nM |
| Ki | 4 | 13 nM | 18 nM | 13 – 50 nM |
| Kd | 4 | 7.1 nM | 7.3 nM | 1.0 – 106 nM |

Representative single records (all retrieved from ChEMBL, assay IDs given so you can cite them):

- **IC50 = 170 nM** — CHEMBL3737992, enzymatic radiometric phosphocellulose paper-disk assay, 0.1 mM EAIYAAPFAKKK peptide substrate, 30 min; pChEMBL 6.77 (doc CHEMBL3734755)
- **IC50 = 19.9 nM** — CHEMBL2406231, TR-FRET, His-ABL 229–513 from *E. coli*, 30–60 min pre-incubation, biotinyl-poly(Glu-Tyr) substrate; pChEMBL 7.70. The ~10× spread vs. the above is the usual ATP-concentration / pre-incubation / substrate dependence
- **Ki = 13 nM** — CHEMBL932076 / CHEMBL962773, filter-binding assay on human recombinant Abl; pChEMBL 7.89
- **Kd = 1.1 nM** — CHEMBL1908688, competition binding against the **non-phosphorylated** ABL1 kinase domain; pChEMBL 8.96. The same study gives Kd = 21 nM for the **phosphorylated** kinase domain — imatinib only binds the inactive/DFG-out conformation, which is the main reason binding and enzymatic numbers diverge
- **Cellular GI50 = 260 nM** — CHEMBL4383405, TEL-ABL-transformed BA/F3 proliferation

## ANSWER

**IC50 = 170 nM** against wild-type human ABL1 (ChEMBL assay CHEMBL3737992; enzymatic radiometric phosphocellulose paper-disk kinase assay, EAIYAAPFAKKK peptide substrate; pChEMBL 6.77).

Consistent alternatives from the same target record (CHEMBL1862 / UniProt P00519, compound CHEMBL941):
- Ki = 13 nM — filter-binding enzyme assay (CHEMBL932076)
- Kd = 1.1 nM — competition binding, non-phosphorylated ABL1 kinase domain (CHEMBL1908688)
